person.fullBio:
The emphasis of my professional career has been public education: as a teacher, school counselor, and associate professor. As a K-12 school counselor, I became interested in higher education training programs for school counselors. My interest continues in that area as I strive to intertwine reality and theory into school counselor education. My research interests include the training of school counselors, the effectiveness of school counselor comprehensive programs in schools, reducing the achievement gap through effective school counselor services and programs.

My passion is children, from birth to old age. Most recently I have been active in grants which involve placing school counselors in elementary schools in the metro area.  These schools have never had the services of school counselors prior to the grant; therefore I am closely monitoring the effectiveness of the services and programs the counselors deliver.  I am also involved in a grant in a high school in the metro area which creates a school counseling position to help students be better prepared for post secondary choices.  Another research activity involves a junior high after-school program to assist low income students in becoming successful students. (See a recent article about the SOAR program.)

Working with and for children of all ages has always been my goal.  I have presented at a national and state conferences on the value of play and humor in groups at all levels of education.  My enthusiasm is for teaching--providing students the challenge to grow, learn and become efficient and expert counselors in our schools.
